title: Wired Logic: AND and OR
description: Two latching switches in series light a red LED only when both are closed, forming an AND gate. Two switches in parallel light a green LED when either is closed, forming an OR gate. Live truth tables highlight the row matching the current switch settings.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Electronics
Electric Circuits
Digital Logic
Boolean Algebra
Switches
prerequisites: How breadboard rows and rails are connected

simulationModel.type: DC node-voltage analysis with iterative nonlinear element resolution
equations: Kirchhoff's current law at every net
I = (Va - Vb - Vf) / R per branch
assumptions: Every frame is DC steady state
LEDs use a fixed forward voltage plus a small series resistance
Components are ideal - no tolerance, temperature, or wire resistance
limitations: No transient response - no charging or discharging over time
Capacitors are open circuits, so RC timing is not modelled
No inductance and no AC sources
Transistor current gain (beta) is not modelled
Switch contact bounce is not modelled - real switches chatter for a few milliseconds on closing
